q: Which describes generative AI compared with traditional ML?
o: Generative AI creates new content; traditional ML mostly classifies or predicts values
Generative AI cannot use neural networks
Traditional ML always needs more data than generative AI
e: Traditional ML predicts labels or numbers. Generative AI produces new text, images, audio or code.

q: A company wants to generate product images from text descriptions. Which kind of model fits?
e: Text-to-image generation uses diffusion models, such as Amazon Nova Canvas and Stable Diffusion models on Bedrock.

q: Which use case is a good fit for a large language model?
o: Controlling a robot arm's motor in real time with hard safety guarantees
Calculating payroll tax to the penny
Counting rows in a database table
e: LLMs excel at language tasks: summarising, drafting, classifying text, Q&A. Exact maths and hard real-time control need deterministic systems.

q: What does 'grounding' mean for a generative AI answer?
o: Tying the answer to trusted source data provided in context
Connecting the server to an electrical earth
Training the model on the ground truth only
e: A grounded answer is based on retrieved or supplied facts rather than the model's memory, which makes it more accurate and checkable.
an: Ask My Data grounds Oracle: it fetches your real recipe and stock rows, then answers from them.

q: Which two settings both make generation less random? (Choose TWO.)
e: Lower temperature and lower top-p (or top-k) narrow the token choices, making output more focused.

q: Why might a company prefer a smaller language model over a larger one?
o: Lower cost and latency for a well-defined task
Smaller models always know more facts
Larger models cannot run on AWS
e: Smaller models are cheaper and faster. If they meet the quality bar for the task, they're the better business choice.

q: What is the role of a vector database in a generative AI application?
o: Storing embeddings and finding the most similar items quickly
e: Vector databases index embeddings for fast similarity search, the retrieval step of RAG.

q: Which AWS services can store and search vector embeddings for generative AI? (Choose TWO.)
e: Vector-capable stores on AWS include OpenSearch (and Serverless), Aurora and RDS PostgreSQL with pgvector, Neptune Analytics and DocumentDB.

q: What is a 'prompt' in generative AI?
o: The input instructions and context given to the model
e: A prompt can include instructions, context, examples, input data and the desired output format.

q: What is a system prompt?
o: Standing instructions that set the model's role, rules and behaviour for the conversation
The operating system of the server
An error message from the API
e: System prompts set persona, constraints and format rules that apply to every turn.
an: Oracle's system prompt plus its SELF_KNOWLEDGE text set who it is and what it knows about RPGACE before you type anything.

q: Which statement about generative AI and explainability is true?
o: It is often hard to explain exactly why a large model produced a specific output
Every output comes with a full logical proof
Explainability is never a concern for regulated industries
Explainability only matters for image models
e: Large models are opaque. Regulated uses need extra transparency: documentation, citations, human review.

q: What is a common way to make an LLM cite where its answer came from?
o: Use RAG and return the source passages with the answer
e: RAG systems (such as Bedrock Knowledge Bases) can return the retrieved sources alongside the answer for citation.

q: Which describes self-supervised learning in foundation model pre-training?
o: The model learns from unlabelled data by predicting hidden or next parts of it
Humans label every sentence by hand
The model is rewarded by a game score
The model copies a smaller model
e: Self-supervised learning creates labels from the data itself, such as predicting the next token.

q: What is reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) used for in LLMs?
o: Aligning model responses with human preferences
e: RLHF uses human rankings of answers to train the model towards helpful, harmless, preferred responses.

q: A model was trained with data up to last year. A user asks about yesterday's news. What is the most likely result without RAG or tools?
o: It cannot know and may hallucinate an answer
It will always say it doesn't know
e: Without retrieval or tools, a model has no access to events after its cut-off and may invent plausible details.
an: That's why RPGACE's web lookups go to a live search instead of trusting Oracle's memory for current facts.

q: Which is a key advantage of using a managed foundation model API?
o: No infrastructure to manage, and pay-as-you-go pricing
Full control of the model's training data
e: Managed APIs remove infrastructure work and let you start small, paying per use.

q: Which describes asynchronous inference for a generative AI workload?
o: Requests are queued and processed in the background, with results collected later
Every request must finish in under 100 ms
Requests are processed only on the user's device
e: Asynchronous patterns suit long-running jobs. The caller doesn't wait on an open connection.
an: Bookworm analyses the rest of a chapter in the background and you see it when it's done, rather than waiting minutes on a spinner.

q: What is streaming output from an LLM?
o: Returning tokens as they are generated, so users see the answer build up
Sending the model weights to the browser
e: Streaming improves perceived latency: the first words appear quickly instead of after the whole answer is ready.
an: Oracle chat streams. RPGACE's server passes the model's stream straight through, so replies appear word by word.

q: Which is an example of a non-deterministic output problem?
o: A test that checks for an exact answer string fails because the model words it differently each time
A database returns the same row every time
A calculator gives the same sum
e: Because generative output varies, test for meaning or structure (or use LLM-as-a-judge), not exact strings.

q: A company wants AI to answer questions about scanned PDF contracts. Which combination makes sense?
o: Amazon Textract to extract the text, then a Bedrock knowledge base for RAG
Amazon Polly to read the PDFs aloud only
e: Extract text from scans first (Textract), then index it for retrieval so a foundation model can answer from it.

q: Which describes a hallucination detection approach?
o: Checking the answer against the retrieved source text to flag unsupported claims
e: Grounding checks compare responses with source material. Bedrock Guardrails offers contextual grounding checks.

q: Which describes an Amazon Nova model?
o: A family of foundation models built by Amazon, available on Amazon Bedrock
e: Amazon Nova covers understanding models (text, image, video input) and creative models (image and video generation) on Bedrock.

q: A model must process images and text together to answer questions about product photos. What capability is required?
e: Multimodal models take image plus text input. Text-only models can't see the photo.

q: Which statement about tokens and cost is correct?
o: Long prompts and long responses both increase cost
Only the number of requests is billed
Tokens are free on all services
e: Both input and output tokens count. Trimming prompts and capping outputs reduces spend.
